newsitem.title: USA: Presidential debate group recommends 'no Perot'.
newsitem.headline: Presidential debate group recommends 'no Perot'.

text.p: A commission planning for the 1996 presidential debates between President Bill Clinton and Republican Bob Dole recommended on Tuesday that Ross Perot and all third-party candidates be excluded.

"The commission unanimously agreed with the unanimous recommendation of our independent advisory committee that only President Clinton and Senator Dole and their running mates be invited to participate," said commission co-chairmen Paul Kirk and Frank Fahrenkopf in a statement announcing the panel's decision.
The recommendation, which won quick endorsement from the Dole campaign but would also need the Clinton team's approval, seemed likely to stir widespread controversy.

Alhough Perot, an outspoken Texas billionaire, has attracted only single-digit poll support so far this year, he was a lively star of the 1992 debates and went on to win 19 percent of the popular vote in the election won by Democrat Clinton.

Perot campaign coordinator Russ Vernery denounced the decision as "a travesty of justice." Perot campaign spokeswoman Sharon Holman said, "It shows the extent to which they are trying to shut us out if indeed this is true."

The Commission on Presidential Debates, chaired by former Democratic Party chairman Kirk and former Republican chairman Fahrenkopf, was formed to take planning for the crucial campaign debates out of the partisan arena.
